articles.description: I recently blogged about the importance of distinct and isolated subsystems where real-time data transactions that apply to a particular business data entity are processed, known as a System of Record. Someone referenced that post and incorrectly implied that I was suggesting a Single Source of Truth. I didn't delve deeper into Single Source of Truth in that post to keep it concise. Still, I was careful to suggest "how important it is to separate operational systems from analytical systems" and that analytical systems "must support multiple independent Systems of Record." And in fact, I diagrammed information refinement and how it progresses within enterprises. That diagram isolated Systems of Record from a Single Source of Truth and isolated Operational Systems from Analytical Systems. In this post, I want to detail how and why a Single Source of Truth is different from Systems of Record.
articles.title: System of Record And Source of Single Truth Are Not The Same

articles.description:
.NET 10 RC1 is here, and it's a monster. Think your code is fast now? Just wait.
The team pulled a Frederic Tudor, the 19th-century "Ice King," compounding thousands of tiny optimizations into a massive performance leap. The JIT is now a wizard at "deabstraction," making your clean, high-level C# run like hand-tuned C.

The real magic trick? Expanded escape analysis. The compiler can now stack-allocate small objects that it proves don't "escape" a method. That means less heap allocation and fewer GC pauses. It's the free performance lunch you were always told doesn't exist. Your app gets faster without you changing a line of code.
articles.title: .NET 10 Release 1: Performance Boosts, Security Upgrades, and Smarter AI

articles.description: DistinctConcurrentBag in Spargine is a thread-safe, unordered collection that ensures uniqueness of elements, preventing duplicates. It offers methods for adding, removing, checking, and enumerating items, making it ideal for concurrent programming in .NET. For blocking behavior with uniqueness, DistinctBlockingCollection is recommended.
articles.title: Boost Your .NET Projects: Ensure Thread-Safe Uniqueness with DistinctConcurrentBag in Spargine

articles.author: fofo
articles.description:
DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS removes all clean data pages from the buffer pool. The next queries hit storage (disk/SSD) instead of memory.

DBCC FREEPROCCACHE removes all compiled plans from the plan cache. Queries across the whole instance must recompile, spiking CPU.
articles.title: SQL Server Myth: “DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS / DBCC FREEPROCCACHE are harmless troubleshooting tools”

articles.title: SQL Server Myth: “TRUNCATE TABLE Is Non-Logged”

articles.description:
Following up on my recent posts about ML-KEM and ML-DSA post-quantum cryptography in .NET using BouncyCastle.NET, I wanted to share an interesting development on the Windows side. Microsoft has recently announced post-quantum cryptography support in Windows through their Cryptography API: Next Generation (CNG) libraries.
This development provides an alternative to third-party libraries for quantum-resistant cryptography on Windows systems. The implementation offers direct OS integration and follows standard .NET patterns for cryptographic operations.
articles.title: ML-KEM and ML-DSA Post-Quantum Cryptography in Windows
